title: Schloss Matzen und Schlosspark Reith
name: Schloss Matzen und Schlosspark Reith
kurzbeschreibung: Schloss Matzen near Reith im Alpbachtal: fortified 12th-century castle and a heritage-protected, freely accessible English landscape park with lakes.
beschreibung:
Overview

The storied Schloss Matzen rises picturesquely on a gentle hill where the Zillertal and Alpbachtal meet the lower Inn Valley, situated in the municipality of Reith im Alpbachtal near Brixlegg. Encircled by a heritage-listed English landscape park spanning more than 15 hectares with ancient giant trees, ponds, and walking trails, the estate ranks as one of Tyrol's most significant and beautiful castle monuments. Together with neighbouring fortresses Lichtenwerth, Neumatzen, and Kropfsberg, Schloss Matzen forms the centrepiece of the historic Tyrolean "four-castle quadrilateral".

Route & Requirements

The origins of the fortress date back to the 12th century: originally built by the Herren von Freundsberg to monitor shipping on the Inn River and control the valley passes, the stronghold was first documented in 1167. In the 16th century, the estate came into the possession of the wealthy Ilsung mining family from Schwaz, who transformed the defensive castle into a magnificent Renaissance palace with an arcaded courtyard. Schloss Matzen owes its present romantic appearance to the von Groote family, who renovated the complex in historicist style in the late 19th century and laid out the renowned Matzenpark: this English landscape garden featuring the idyllic Löwenteich (Lion Pond) and Karpfenteich (Carp Pond) is home to rare exotic conifers, giant sequoias, and tranquil avenues. Today, the castle operates as an exclusive boutique hotel, while the expansive castle park remains publicly and freely accessible year-round, captivating nature lovers, walkers, and photographers.

Visit & Arrival

The sprawling Schlosspark Matzen is open during daylight hours all year round with completely free admission (€0.00 admission). The interior rooms of the castle are reserved for hotel and restaurant guests, but the historic castle courtyard and Restaurant Gut Matzen are welcoming to visitors. Getting there by public transport: take the ÖBB train (S-Bahn or REX) to Bahnhof Brixlegg, from where a level, signposted footpath leads directly into the park in about 15 minutes (approx. 1 km); alternatively, take VVT bus route 4074 to the stop Matzen Park. By car: via the Inntalautobahn A12, exit Kramsach/Brixlegg, continue on the B171 Tiroler Straße towards Schwaz; a large pay-and-display visitor car park is situated right at the park entrance.

Tips

The wide, gravelled circular trails through the castle park are completely level and wonderfully suited for pushchairs, wheelchair users, and seniors. A large adventure playground within the park delights families with children. Take a leisurely walk past neighbouring moated Schloss Lichtenwerth and stop by Restaurant Gut Matzen to enjoy Tyrolean culinary delicacies in the shaded chestnut garden.
